mainTopic: The end of the ברייתא on a child's stages, the close of פרק לולב הגזול, and the opening משנה of פרק לולב וערבה on how many days each סוכות מצוה lasts and the לולב on שבת.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that lists the stages of a growing child, where each new ability brings a new law. A child who knows how to slaughter may have his שחיטה eaten, and רב הונא adds that a גדול must supervise. Once a child can eat a כזית of grain, one must keep four אמות from his waste before praying. רב חסדא adds that he must eat it within כדי אכילת פרס, and רב חייא בריה דרב ייבא says an adult's waste counts even without that condition. A child who can eat a כזית of roasted meat may be counted for the קרבן פסח, but רבי יהודה requires that he can also tell food from non-food. Then comes the הדרן for פרק לולב הגזול. A new פרק opens with a משנה listing how many days each סוכות מצוה lasts, and it explains when the לולב and ערבה are done six or seven days. It describes how the לולב was handled in the מקדש when the first day fell on שבת, and how בית דין moved the מצוה home because of the danger. The גמרא asks why the לולב does not always override שבת, and רבה begins to answer with a גזירה that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A child who knows how to slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its list of a child's stages. If a קטן knows how to slaughter, we may eat from his שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a child knows how to slaughter, we may eat from the animals he slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues its list of a child's stages. This stage says that a קטן who knows how to do שחיטה properly can slaughter, and the meat is kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we might think a קטן cannot be trusted with an important halachic act like שחיטה. The ברייתא says that if he truly knows how to do it, his שחיטה is valid. The next step will add a condition.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child below the age of מצוות
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: One who knows how to slaughter —
phrases.notes: This refers to the קטן, continuing the list of the ברייתא

phrases.english: we eat from his slaughtering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא's list of a child's stages on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן who knows how to slaughter may slaughter, and his שחיטה may be eaten.

steps.title: רב הונא: an adult must supervise
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא limits the ruling. The child's שחיטה is only valid if a גדול stands over him and watches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: This applies only if an adult is standing over him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds a condition to the ברייתא. The child's שחיטה is good only when an adult watches him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing how to slaughter is not enough on its own. Since a קטן is not fully reliable, an adult must watch to make sure he slaughtered correctly. This changes the ruling from 'always allowed' to 'allowed only with supervision'.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
And that is provided that an adult is standing over him.
phrases.notes: The adult checks that the שחיטה was done properly

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וְהוּא שֶׁגָּדוֹל עוֹמֵד עַל גַּבָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limiting condition to the ruling of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטן's שחיטה is valid only under an adult's supervision.

steps.title: A child who can eat an olive-bulk of grain
steps.stepSummary: Once a child can eat a כזית of grain, his waste is treated like an adult's. One must distance himself four אמות from it before תפילה or קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he can eat an olive-bulk of grain, we distance ourselves four cubits from his feces and urine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the next stage of the child. Once he eats real grain food, his waste smells like an adult's, so one may not pray near it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A baby's waste is not considered offensive. Once the child eats a כזית of grain, his waste counts as offensive. The law of keeping four אמות away before praying then applies.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, a basic halachic measure of eating

phrases.english: If he is able to eat an olive-bulk of grain —
we distance ourselves from his feces and from his urine
phrases.notes: Before praying or saying קריאת שמע

phrases.english: four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's list with a new stage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once a child can eat a כזית of grain, one must distance himself four אמות from his waste before praying.

steps.title: רב חסדא: within the time of eating a half-loaf
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds that the child must be able to eat the כזית within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: This is provided that he can eat it within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא sets a time limit. The child must be able to finish the כזית of grain within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the child eats very slowly, his body is not yet eating like an adult's. In that case his waste is not yet treated as offensive. Only a child who eats a normal amount in normal time crosses this stage.

keyTerms.meaning: The time it takes to eat a half-loaf, a standard halachic time span

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
And that is provided that he is able to eat it
within the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וְהוּא שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְאוֹכְלוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ruling of step 3 with a time condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The child's waste is treated as offensive only if he can eat a כזית within כדי אכילת פרס.

steps.title: רב חייא: an adult needs no time condition
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב ייבא says that for a גדול, one must distance himself from his waste even if he eats slowly. He brings a פסוק from קהלת as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בריה דרב ייבא said: For an adult, even if he cannot eat it within the time of a half-loaf, one must still distance. As it is written: 'He who increases knowledge increases pain.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חייא explains that רב חסדא's time condition only applies to a child. An adult's waste is always offensive, and he supports this with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The time test is meant to show whether a child's body has matured. An adult is already mature, so the test is irrelevant to him. The פסוק 'יוסיף דעת יוסיף מכאוב' teaches that as a person grows older, his body becomes more flawed, so his waste is offensive no matter how he eats.

keyTerms.meaning: He who increases knowledge increases pain (קהלת א:יח)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two different tests here. For a child, his waste matters once he can eat a כזית of grain within כדי אכילת פרס. For an adult, his waste always matters, with no time condition.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya son of Rav Yeiva said:

phrases.aramaic: וּבַגָּדוֹל, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל
phrases.english: And with an adult, even though he is not able
to eat within the time of eating a half-loaf —
phrases.notes: One must still distance himself from his waste

phrases.english: as it is written:
"And he who increases knowledge increases pain."
phrases.notes: As a person ages, his body becomes more flawed

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יֵיבָא: וּבַגָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב חסדא's time condition does not apply to adults.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For an adult, one must distance himself from his waste even if he eats slowly.

steps.title: A child who can eat an olive-bulk of roasted meat
steps.stepSummary: A child who can eat a כזית of roasted meat may be counted for the קרבן פסח. The source is the פסוק 'איש לפי אכלו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he can eat an olive-bulk of roasted meat, we slaughter the פסח offering on his behalf, as it says: 'Every man according to his eating.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the last stage of its list. A child who can eat a כזית of roasted meat may be included in a group for the קרבן פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says people are counted for the פסח 'according to his eating'. So the test is the ability to eat the required amount, a כזית of the roasted פסח meat. A child who can do that may be counted.

keyTerms.meaning: We slaughter on his behalf, counting him in the group
Every man according to his eating (שמות יב:ד)

phrases.english: If he is able to eat an olive-bulk of roasted meat —
we slaughter the Pesach offering on his behalf,
phrases.notes: He is counted as a member of the group

phrases.english: as it is said: "Every man according to his eating."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא's list with a new stage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A child who can eat a כזית of roasted meat may be counted for the קרבן פסח.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the child must recognize food
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says eating ability is not enough. The child must be able to tell food apart from non-food: he throws away a pebble and takes a nut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: Not until he can discern what is food. How so? They give him a pebble and he throws it away, a nut and he takes it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא. He adds a stricter test before a child may be counted for the פסח, and then explains how that test works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, being able to eat a כזית is enough. רבי יהודה requires real understanding of what eating is. He defines this practically: the child rejects a pebble and accepts a nut, which shows he knows what food is.
steps.confusionAlert: 'כיצד' is not the גמרא asking a question. It is part of רבי יהודה's own statement in the ברייתא, where he explains his own test.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Not until he is able to discern eating.
phrases.notes: He must know what food is

phrases.english: How so?
They give him a pebble — and he throws it away,
a nut — and he takes it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְבָרֵר אֲכִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 6 and requires a stricter test for the פסח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a child is counted for the פסח only when he can tell food apart from non-food.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק לולב הגזול
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of פרק לולב הגזול, the third פרק of מסכת סוכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק לולב הגזול ('A Stolen לולב').
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the פרק with the traditional הדרן, a promise to come back and learn it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not part of the legal discussion. It marks the end of the פרק that dealt with the laws of לולב and the ארבעה מינים.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing formula of a פרק
A stolen לולב, the name of the third פרק of סוכה

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק ends with a list of a child's stages. Each new ability brings new laws: שחיטה with supervision, distancing from his waste, and being counted for the פסח.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter "A Stolen Lulav"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the ברייתא ends.

steps.title: New chapter opens: how many days each סוכות מצוה lasts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opening פרק לולב וערבה lists the number of days for each סוכות מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: לולב and ערבה: six or seven days. הלל and שמחה: eight days. סוכה and ניסוך המים: seven days. The חליל: five or six days.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה. It gives a quick list of how many days each special סוכות מצוה is done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some מצוות have a fixed number of days. הלל and שמחה last eight days, because they include שמיני עצרת. סוכה and ניסוך המים last seven days. Other מצוות say 'six or seven' or 'five or six', because the count changes depending on whether a certain day falls on שבת, when the מצוה may not be done.

keyTerms.meaning: The willow branch used to circle the מִזְבֵּחַ in the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
The praise of תְּהִלִּים recited on יוֹם טוֹב
The מצוה of rejoicing, done by eating the meat of שַׁלְמֵי שִׂמְחָה
Pouring water on the מִזְבֵּחַ during סוּכּוֹת
Flute played in the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ at שִׂמְחַת בֵּית הַשּׁוֹאֵבָה

steps.confusionAlert: 'שִׁשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעָה' does not mean 'six and seven' added together. It means six OR seven, depending on how the calendar falls that year.
steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the outline for the whole פרק. The rest of the פרק explains each item one by one.

phrases.english: Lulav and willow — six or seven days.
phrases.notes: The number depends on which day falls on שבת.

phrases.english: Hallel and rejoicing — eight days.
phrases.notes: The seven days of סוכות plus שמיני עצרת.

phrases.english: Sukkah and the water libation — seven days.
The flute — five or six days.
phrases.notes: It is not played on שבת, and not on יום טוב either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק right after the הדרן of פרק לולב הגזול in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each סוכות מצוה has a set number of days: לולב and ערבה 6 or 7, הלל and שמחה 8, סוכה and ניסוך המים 7, חליל 5 or 6.

steps.title: When the לולב is taken all seven days
steps.stepSummary: לולב is taken seven days only when the first day of the חג falls on שבת. Otherwise it is taken six days.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can לולב be seven days? If the first day of the חג falls on שבת, the לולב is taken all seven days. If the first day falls on any other day, it is taken only six days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains its own words 'six or seven' for the לולב. It asks 'כיצד?' and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day, taking the לולב is a מצוה מן התורה, so it is done even on שבת. On the other days it is only a מצוה מדרבנן, and it is not done on שבת. So if שבת is on the first day, no day is lost and the count is seven. If שבת falls later in the week, that day is skipped and the count is six.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? The משנה uses it to introduce an explanation of its own words
The first day of the חג

phrases.english: Lulav seven days — how so?
If the first day of the Festival
happens to fall on Shabbat —
the lulav is taken seven days,
phrases.notes: On the first day the מצוה is from the Torah, so it overrides שבת.

phrases.english: and in all other cases — six days.
phrases.notes: שבת falls on a day when the מצוה is only rabbinic, so that day is skipped.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the 'six or seven' for לולב from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לולב is taken seven days only when the first day of the חג falls on שבת. Otherwise it is taken six days.

steps.title: When the ערבה ritual is done all seven days
steps.stepSummary: The ערבה is done seven days only when the seventh day of ערבה falls on שבת. Otherwise it is done six days.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can ערבה be seven days? If the seventh day of ערבה falls on שבת, the ערבה is done all seven days. In all other cases it is done six days.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same 'כיצד' pattern to explain 'six or seven' for the ערבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the לולב, but in reverse. For ערבה, the special day that overrides שבת is the seventh day (הושענא רבה), not the first. So if שבת falls on the seventh day, nothing is skipped. If שבת falls on another day, that day is skipped.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh day of the ערבה מצוה, known as הוֹשַׁעְנָא רַבָּה

steps.confusionAlert: For לולב, the day that overrides שבת is the FIRST day. For ערבה, it is the SEVENTH day. Do not mix them up.

phrases.english: Willow seven days — how so?
If the seventh day of the willow
happens to fall on Shabbat —
the willow is done seven days,
and in all other cases — six days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 10, now applied to the ערבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערבה overrides שבת only on its seventh day. So it is done seven days only when that day falls on שבת.

steps.title: How the לולב was handled in the בית המקדש when the first day fell on שבת
steps.stepSummary: People brought their לולבים to the הר הבית before שבת. On שבת morning each person took whichever לולב reached him, and everyone declared ahead of time that his לולב is a gift to whoever gets it.
steps.simpleTranslation: How was the לולב מצוה done when the first day of the חג fell on שבת? Everyone brought their לולבים to the הר הבית. The attendants took them and arranged them on a bench. The זקנים put theirs in a special room. The people were taught to say: 'Whoever ends up with my לולב, it is his as a gift.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the practical procedure for the case from step 10, when the first day falls on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking the לולב overrides שבת, but carrying it through the street does not. So the לולבים were brought to the הר הבית before שבת, on ערב שבת. On the first day you must own your לולב ('ולקחתם לכם'). Since people would grab whichever לולב they found in the rush, everyone gave his לולב as a gift, so whoever took it would own it. The זקנים kept theirs in a room so they would not get hurt in the crowd.

keyTerms.meaning: A chamber or room in the בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
As a gift, which gives the receiver real ownership

steps.whatToRemember: On the first day of סוכות the לולב must belong to you. So when everyone's לולבים got mixed together, each person gave his לולב as a gift to whoever took it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for a key practical rule: on the first day you cannot use a borrowed לולב, but you can use one that was given to you as a gift.

phrases.english: The מצוה of lulav — how is it done on Shabbat?
When the first day of the Festival
happens to fall on Shabbat
they bring their lulavim to the Temple Mount,
phrases.notes: They did this on Friday, before שבת began.

phrases.english: and the attendants receive them from them
and arrange them on top of a bench,
and the elders place theirs in a chamber.
phrases.notes: So they would not be hurt in the morning crowd.

phrases.english: And they teach them to say:
Anyone into whose hand my lulav comes —
it is his as a gift.
phrases.notes: On the first day the לולב must belong to the one using it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical procedure for the case in step 10, when the first day falls on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the first day falls on שבת, לולבים were brought to the הר הבית beforehand, and everyone gave his לולב as a gift so that whoever took it would own it.

steps.title: The crowd grabs for the לולבים, so בית דין moves the מצוה home
steps.stepSummary: The משנה describes how the attendants threw the לולבים into the crowd, which led to grabbing and hitting. בית דין responded with a תקנה that each person takes his לולב in his own house.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day they got up early and came. The attendants threw the לולבים in front of them, and the people grabbed them and hit one another. When בית דין saw that this was leading to danger, they made a rule that each person should take his לולב in his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the story from the last step. It tells what happened on שבת morning in the מקדש and how בית דין changed the practice because people were getting hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old system had a real problem. Throwing the לולבים into the crowd led to grabbing and fights. So בית דין used their authority to make a תקנה. People would no longer collect their לולבים at the הר הבית, and each person would take his לולב at home.

keyTerms.meaning: The attendants or officials of the מקדש (not the modern meaning of 'cantor')
They made a rabbinic rule (a תַּקָּנָה)

steps.whatToRemember: Taking the לולב on a שבת first day used to be done as a group on the הר הבית. Because the crowd became dangerous, בית דין moved it into each person's home.
steps.confusionAlert: Here חַזָּנִין means the attendants of the מקדש. It does not mean the prayer leaders we call 'chazzanim' today.

phrases.english: The next day they rise early and come,
phrases.notes: 'The next day' is the שבת morning, after the לולבים were brought on Friday.

phrases.english: and the attendants throw them (the lulavim) before them,
and they snatch them
and strike one another.
phrases.notes: In the rush to grab a לולב, people end up hitting each other.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁרָאוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁבָּאוּ לִידֵי סַכָּנָה —
phrases.english: And when the court saw that they came to danger —

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהֵא כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹטֵל בְּבֵיתוֹ.
phrases.english: they instituted that each and every one take it in his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁרָאוּ בֵּית דִּין שֶׁבָּאוּ לִידֵי סַכָּנָה הִתְקִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's story from step 12 about bringing the לולבים to the הר הבית before שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because of the danger caused by the crowd grabbing לולבים, בית דין ruled that each person takes his לולב at home on a שבת first day.

steps.title: Why doesn't the לולב override שבת if taking it is only moving it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why taking a לולב is ever forbidden on שבת. Picking it up is just moving an object, so the מצוה should push שבת aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Why? Taking a לולב is just moving something around, so let it push aside שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a challenge to the משנה's rule that the לולב is not taken on every שבת. It argues that the act is so minor that the מצוה should win.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picking up a לולב is not one of the Torah's forbidden מלאכות. It is only טלטול, simply moving an object. A Torah מצוה should be stronger than such a small issue. So the rule that the לולב does not override שבת seems to need an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Moving or carrying an object around (not a real מְלָאכָה)
Let it push aside or override

phrases.english: GEMARA: Why?
phrases.notes: Why is the לולב not taken on שבת, as the משנה said?

phrases.english: It is merely moving an object,
so let it override Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי טִלְטוּל בְּעָלְמָא הוּא וְלִידְחֵי שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא by questioning the משנה's basic rule that the לולב does not always override שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule (step 10) that the לולב is not taken on שבת except in limited cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taking a לולב involves only טלטול, not a real מלאכה. A Torah מצוה should therefore override such a minor issue.

steps.title: רבה: a rabbinic decree in case one carries the לולב to an expert
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that the חכמים made a גזירה. They feared a person would take the לולב in his hand and go to an expert to learn how to do the מצוה. The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is a decree, in case a person takes the לולב in his hand and goes to an expert to learn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins to explain why the לולב does not override שבת. The reason is a rabbinic גזירה, a protective fence. His sentence is not finished yet; the end of it comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה agrees that the act of taking the לולב is not a problem in itself. The worry is what might happen next. Someone who does not know how to do the מצוה could carry the לולב to an expert, and carrying through a public area is a real Torah prohibition. So the חכמים stopped the whole מצוה on שבת to protect against that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: A protective rabbinic decree that prevents a possible violation
An expert, someone who knows the laws well

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying that taking the לולב is itself a forbidden act on שבת. The concern is that the person might carry it, and the גזירה protects against that.
steps.whyThisMatters: The same reasoning is used for שופר on ראש השנה and מגילה on פורים when they fall on שבת. This is why we don't take the לולב on שבת today.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
It is a decree lest he take it in his hand
and go to an expert to learn,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud, which explains the danger of carrying in public.
